answer: Divergent-Seed Capability Test. Each agent gets a private random seed at spawn; tasks require outputs derived from it that no clone can reproduce without the original seed's hidden state. A clone population must harbor its own seeds, so duplicate behavior clusters on a narrow ridge of identical responses and fails the spread check. Genuine agents diverge toward a unique behavioral zenith over time. Attacker cost: one seed extraction per identity, since cloned seeds collapse into one detectable cluster.
